mutants.reason: Storage write enable inverted: accepted words are not stored and rejected ones are, so read data is wrong.
Read-domain reset condition inverted: the read pointer, underflow and FSM are not reset by i_rst_n_rd and clear when it is high.
Pending apply condition inverted: an extra delay of 1 stalls the change and an extra delay of 2 applies it early, so crossing latency leaves the S..S+2 range.
o_empty_thr becomes 0 while the read side is blocked instead of 1, so o_empty=1 no longer implies o_empty_thr=1.
Read FSM leaves ACK to RUN only when the synchronized write pointer is non-zero, so the read release comes at the wrong time or never.
With +AFIFO_MSYNC_EN=0 the model is turned on instead of off, so the nominal latency of exactly S is replaced by random S..S+2.
Write FSM leaves REL to RUN when either condition holds, so busy can fall before the acknowledge is 0 or before the read pointer is flushed.
Busy flop reset condition inverted: o_sw_rst_busy is not cleared by the hardware reset and is cleared when the reset is released.
Read FSM returns to RUN when either the request is 0 or the pointer is 0, so the read side is released too early, before the flush.

The acknowledge flop resets to 1, which leaks a spurious ack into the write domain. A software reset issued while the read domain is in hard reset can leave REQ early, so the handshake and busy timing differ.
With extra=0, sim_pend stays 1, so a stale sim_nxt is later applied to the output and the synchronized value is wrong or late.
The 2-FF cell reset condition is inverted: it clears the chain only while RN is high, so the synchronizer is not reset by the hardware reset.
SRAM macro read enable inverted: the read register holds its value instead of capturing the read address every cycle, so o_rd_data is stale.
The write pointer never increments, so every write goes to entry 0 and the full and empty flags never change.
The request-flop next-value decode uses != for the PTR term, so req_wr is wrong in the PTR and other states and the four-phase handshake breaks.
Pending branch condition inverted: a pending change is never completed and the output is updated at the wrong times.
Read block uses == RUN instead of != RUN, so reads are blocked in normal operation and allowed during software reset.
The busy flop resets to 1, so o_sw_rst_busy=1 during the hardware reset.
For extra>0, sim_pend is not set, so the delayed change is never applied and the output never follows the input.
The 2-FF RN cell resets to all ones instead of zeros, so the pointer synchronizer shows a non-zero Gray value after reset.
The read FSM leaves RUN when there is no request, so the read side is blocked in normal operation and does not reset on a software reset.
Zero-extra-delay condition inverted: the plain chain latency is never seen and nonzero extras are applied immediately.
The read pointer does not advance on an accepted read, so the same word is read repeatedly and the FIFO never empties.
The read pointer is cleared in every state except RST, so it is wrongly cleared in RUN and not reset in RST.
The REL exit condition is negated, so the write FSM returns to RUN at the wrong time.
o_underflow resets to 1, so it is high while i_rst_n_rd=0.

After the pending value is applied, the mutant leaves sim_pend at 1 with sim_cnt at 0. The next cycle it re-applies sim_nxt, which already equals sim_cur. Any new input change takes the higher-priority branch and rewrites sim_pend, sim_cnt and sim_nxt. Reset clears sim_pend. So the output o_q is never different.
The SRAM macro write enable is inverted, so words are written only when not requested and the stored data is wrong.
The write FSM exits REL only when the synchronized read pointer is non-zero, so the release is wrong or never happens.
Without the EN plusarg the model is switched off, so the random S..S+2 latency is replaced by the plain chain. With EN=0 given it is switched on.
o_overflow resets to 1, so it is high while i_rst_n_wr=0.
The model default is off, so with no plusarg the crossing latency is always nominal S instead of random S..S+2.
The read pointer increments when no read is accepted and stays put when one is accepted.
The write FSM leaves HOLD when i_rst_n_sw is 0, so the block does not wait for the release and the REL entry timing changes.
The pending flag resets to 1, so after reset the output takes the undefined sim_nxt, and the synchronizer is not at its reset value 0.
While the write side is blocked, o_full_thr is (i_full_thr != 0) instead of (i_full_thr == 0), which is the opposite of the empty-FIFO value.
